identity.title: [v0.92.1][GCP-D1] Deploy the bounded private foundation and prove non-GPU workload disposal

values.summary: After recovering stale #731 review/publication truth for PR #739, the current follow-up remediation tightened the live GCP scripts and added no-live behavioral guard evidence for the review blockers. Mutation authorization fails closed on expired deadlines, approvals older than 120 minutes, cleanup windows over 30 minutes, and non-service-account impersonation identities. The disposable workload script now arms cleanup before the create attempt, uses an EXIT cleanup trap plus independent deadline reaper, proves guest readiness/metadata identity, enumerates expanded zero-residue surfaces including forwarding rules, firewall overrides, VM-specific IAM, Terraform state run labels, and storage objects/all versions, and fails closed on injected post-create, partial-create, and storage-residue cases. The foundation apply script now uses service-account impersonation, exact project/subnet/firewall/OS Login/IAM/bucket/logging readbacks, and rollback-on-failure. No new live GCP mutation was run during this remediation; earlier retained live foundation/workload evidence remains historical evidence only, and any fresh live rerun requires a new unexpired operator authorization packet.
actual_changes: Recovered #731 from the stale PR #739 review/publication state before editing.

Tightened .csdlc/prepared/issues/731/validate-gcp-d1-authorization-packet.sh to require an unexpired cleanup deadline, approved_at_utc when approved, approval age no greater than 120 minutes, cleanup lifetime no greater than 30 minutes, and a service-account impersonation identity.

Tightened .csdlc/prepared/issues/731/run-gcp-d1-disposable-workload-proof.sh to validate authorization before mutation, arm cleanup before the VM create attempt, arm an independent deadline reaper, trap failures with cleanup deletion, prove guest readiness and metadata service-account identity, enumerate storage objects/all versions from the accepted foundation buckets, and check forwarding rules, firewall overrides, VM-specific IAM, storage-object, and Terraform-state run-label residue in addition to instances, disks, and addresses.

Tightened .csdlc/prepared/issues/731/run-gcp-d1-foundation-apply-and-readback.sh to obtain Terraform access through --impersonate-service-account, trap failed apply/readback with terraform destroy rollback, and assert exact project metadata, workload service account, firewall denominator, IAM, bucket labels, and logging metric readbacks.

Added and expanded .csdlc/prepared/issues/731/validate-gcp-d1-remediation-guards.sh with retained .csdlc/evidence/731/remediation-guards/** proving the new guards without live GCP mutation, including synthetic rejected packets, success-path workload readiness/residue execution, storage-residue rejection, partial-create cleanup, injected post-create cleanup, foundation readback success, and injected foundation rollback.
Preserved the historical live GCP evidence directories without overwriting them during no-live mock validation.

actual_validation.purpose: Prove the #731 PR #739 remediation fail-closed guards without live GCP mutation: fresh/expired authorization, 30-minute cleanup cap, service-account impersonation identity, success-path workload readiness and expanded zero residue, storage object/all-version residue rejection, partial-create cleanup, injected post-create cleanup, foundation readback success, and injected foundation rollback.
Retain traced no-live remediation guard provenance for the current script state.
